title: Négritude movement
summary: The Négritude movement formed in Paris between the wars among three young students: Aimé Césaire of Martinique, Léopold Sédar Senghor of Senegal and Léon-Gontran Damas of Guiana. Having met in Paris in 1931, they began publishing the journal L'Étudiant noir in 1934, the first journal devoted to Négritude.

uncertainty.note: Poets.org gives 1934 for the first publication of L'Étudiant noir; the Assemblée nationale page shows a March 1935 issue.

as_recorded.value: began to publish the first journal devoted to Négritude, L’Étudiant noir (The Black Student), in 1934

importance.justification: The movement gave Black francophone writers a shared literary and political voice in the colonial era.

sources.title: Aimé Césaire et le mouvement de la négritude
sources.author: Assemblée nationale

reviewer_note: The two pages differ on the first issue (1934 vs a March 1935 issue shown). The Assemblée nationale page says only that the movement formed in Paris between the wars.
